newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania c.bank refinancing loans down in May.
newsitem.headline: Romania c.bank refinancing loans down in May.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) refinancing loans fell by 16.25 percent last month after a 12.6 percent drop in April when the BNR gave up its auctioned credits facility, data showed on Tuesday.

The total daily refinancing was 4.32 trillion lei on average in May, when Lombard loans plunged to 0.2 billion lei from 13.2 billion the previous month amid an overliquid money market due to BNR purchases of dollar excess.
The BNR made some pilot deals with government securities last month to mop up excess of leu funds but its limited treasury bill portfolio prevented it from sterilising the excess of money supply.

On Monday, the BNR started to drain leu liquidity excess after the government allowed it last week to take deposits from banks as an initial step to implement open-market operations in conducting monetary policy.
Structural refinancing facilities, for which the BNR charges a discount rate of 50 percent, went up to 2.4 trillion lei in May from some 2.2 trillion lei the previous month.

Credits granted to debtors in dispute at law, respectively to troubled banks Dacia Felix SA and Renasterea Creditului Romanesc Credit Bank SA, stayed frozen at 1.88 billion lei. The BNR does not charge interest on loans to those debtors.
Both banks, which revealed big debts and huge losses, await court ruling on their reorganisation or liquidation.
